terms.modal.title: Terms of Use
terms.modal.subtitle: Please read these terms before using Calm Down.
terms.b1: Calm Down is a personal wellness tool designed to support stress management and emotional regulation. It is not a medical service, mental health treatment, or clinical intervention. Nothing in this app constitutes medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
terms.h2: Not a Substitute for Professional Care
terms.b2: If you are experiencing a mental health crisis, please contact a qualified professional or call/text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline). This app is not a replacement for therapy, counseling, or any other professional care.
terms.b3: The tools and exercises in this app are provided as general wellness resources. Results vary by individual. You are responsible for determining whether any tool is appropriate for your situation.
terms.b4: This app is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. We make no guarantees about outcomes, availability, or fitness for any particular purpose.
privacy.modal.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.modal.subtitle: Your privacy is a core principle of this app — not an afterthought.
privacy.notice: We collect absolutely nothing. No account, no login, no tracking.
privacy.b1: Calm Down does not collect, store, or transmit any personal information. Your stress levels, written responses, and session activity never leave your device.
privacy.b2: All session data lives only in your browser tab. When you close or refresh the tab, everything is gone. Nothing is written to cookies, local storage, or any server.
privacy.b3: If you choose to download your responses, that file is saved only to your device using your browser's standard download function. We never see it.
privacy.b4: This app contains no analytics scripts, ad trackers, or third-party services of any kind. There is nothing here watching you.
attribution.modal.title: Attribution
attribution.h1: The Calm Toolkit by Marriage Helper
attribution.b1: The tools, frameworks, and therapeutic concepts in this app — the PIES categories, the stress scale, and the calm-down exercises — are drawn from The Calm Toolkit by Marriage Helper.
attribution.b2: Marriage Helper is a resource dedicated to helping individuals and couples navigate difficult seasons with evidence-based tools and compassionate guidance. Their work is the foundation this app is built on, and we are genuinely grateful for it.
attribution.b3: Learn more at marriagehelper.com.
attribution.b4: Calm Down is an independent personal project built by a Marriage Helper community member to make these tools more accessible in a private, offline-capable digital format. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or a product of Marriage Helper.
attribution.b5: No data is ever collected or transmitted. Everything stays on your device.
version.modal.title: Build Version
stress.desc.1: A little uneasy — something's on your mind.
stress.desc.3: Low stress — off but still functioning.
stress.desc.4: Noticeable anxiety — thoughts starting to race.
stress.desc.5: Moderate stress — harder to focus and settle.
stress.desc.6: Anxious and overwhelmed — difficult to think clearly.
stress.desc.7: High stress — body and mind both affected.
stress.desc.8: Significant distress — hard to function normally.
stress.desc.10: Complete overwhelm — hard to function at all.
category.physical.label: Physical
category.physical.desc: My body feels tense, tired, or out of control. I'm not sleeping or eating well.
category.mental.label: Intellectual (Mental)
category.mental.desc: My thoughts are racing. I can't think clearly or stop worrying.
category.emotional.label: Emotional
category.emotional.desc: My feelings are overwhelming me. I feel hopeless, sad, or like I'm drowning.
category.spiritual.label: Spiritual
category.spiritual.desc: I feel disconnected from what matters. I've lost my sense of peace and purpose.

affirmation.faith.1: God, help me. I need you right now.
affirmation.faith.2: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
affirmation.faith.3: The Lord is close to the brokenhearted.
affirmation.faith.4: Be still and know that I am God.
affirmation.faith.5: Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.
affirmation.faith.6: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give you.
affirmation.universal.3: I am stronger than this moment.
affirmation.universal.7: I have survived every hard thing until now.
affirmation.universal.8: I am enough as I am.
affirmation.universal.10: I choose to take this one breath at a time.
box-breathing.title: Box Breathing
box-breathing.subtitle: 4-count breathing — activates your calm response
box-breathing.extended-exhale: Extended Exhale Mode — shifts to a 6-count exhale for a deeper calm effect
box-breathing.coaching: Try to breathe into your whole trunk — chest AND belly. Place one hand on your chest and one on your stomach to feel both expand.
ftb.title: Full Trunk Deep Breathing
ftb.subtitle: Body-awareness breathing — chest, belly, and back
ftb.step1: Find a comfortable position — lying down is ideal, but sitting works too.
ftb.step2: Place one hand on your chest and one on your belly.
ftb.step3: When you breathe in, feel BOTH your chest and your belly expand. Your back should expand too.
ftb.step.label: Step {n}
ftb.read-hint: Read the instruction, then tap Next when ready.
ftb.complete: Four full cycles complete. Your body is calmer than it was a few minutes ago.
growth.title: Growth Mindset Reframe
growth.subtitle: Fixed thought → growth question
growth.q.label: Question {n} of {total}
growth.q1: What is the thought that is overwhelming you right now?
growth.q1.hint: (You don't have to type it — just hold it in mind.)
growth.q2: Is this a permanent fact, or is it a temporary situation?
growth.q3: What is one thing within this situation that you DO have control over?
growth.q4: What could this experience be teaching you, even if it is painful?
growth.q5: Write down or hold in mind one small action you can take today that is within your control.
growth.placeholder: Your thoughts (optional — nothing is saved or transmitted)
growth.affirmation: You are not stuck. You are in a moment that will pass. Growth happens in hard seasons.
habit.title: Habit Loop Audit
habit.intro: A habit loop has three parts: a Trigger (what sets it off), a Behavior (what you do), and a Result (what you feel after).
habit.trigger.label: Your Trigger
habit.trigger.q: What is your trigger right now?
habit.trigger.hint: A feeling, a time of day, a place, a person?
habit.behavior.label: Your Behavior
habit.behavior.q: What behavior do you default to when that trigger hits?
habit.result.label: The Result
habit.result.q: What is the short-term result? What is the long-term result?
habit.replacement.label: Replacement
habit.replacement.q: What is a healthier behavior you could try instead the next time this trigger appears?
habit.placeholder: Write it out (nothing is saved or transmitted)
habit.affirmation: You don't have to fix the whole loop today. Just noticing it is the first step.
gratitude.title: Focus on the Good
gratitude.framing: This is not about denying that things are hard. It is about reminding your brain that hard is not the whole picture.
gratitude.q.label: Question {n} of {total}
gratitude.q1: What is one thing that happened today that was not terrible — even if it was small?
gratitude.q2: Who is one person in your life who is on your side?
gratitude.q3: What is one thing about yourself you are not giving yourself credit for right now?
gratitude.placeholder: Take your time (nothing is saved or transmitted)
gratitude.affirmation: Your brain needed that. Come back here any time.
ntl.title: Name the Lie, Say the Truth
ntl.framing: Right now you are probably telling yourself things that are not true. Let's look at one of them.
ntl.step1.label: Step 1 of 4
ntl.step1.q: What is the harshest thing you are currently saying to yourself?
ntl.step1.placeholder: Write it down. You don't have to share it with anyone. Nothing is saved or transmitted.
ntl.step2.label: Step 2 of 4
ntl.step2.sub: Now ask: Is this statement 100% true, or is it a story I am telling myself?
ntl.step3.label: Step 3 of 4
ntl.step3.q: What would you say to your best friend if they said this to you?
ntl.step3.placeholder: Write what you'd say to someone you love. Nothing is saved or transmitted.
ntl.step4.label: Step 4 of 4
ntl.step4.sub: Not a fake positive spin — the actual truth about yourself and this situation.
ntl.affirmation: That truth is the thing worth listening to.
resourcing.title: Safe Place Visualization
resourcing.framing: Close your eyes after reading each step. Take your time.
resourcing.step1: Think of a place — real or imagined — where you feel completely safe and at peace.
resourcing.step2: What does it look like? Notice the colors, the light.
resourcing.step3: What sounds are there? Or is it quiet?
resourcing.step4: Feel the temperature. Feel the surface beneath you.
resourcing.step5: You are here. Nothing can reach you in this place. Stay as long as you need.
resourcing.hold.label: You are safe. Stay here.
resourcing.affirmation: When you are ready, take a slow breath and come back.
mantra.title: Positive Mantra
mantra.subtitle: Select a phrase or write your own
mantra.faith.label: Faith-Based
mantra.universal.label: Universal
mantra.custom.label: Your own phrase
mantra.session.hint: Read it slowly. Read it again. Breathe between each reading.
prayer.title: Prayer Prompt
prayer.framing: Prayer does not have to be long or eloquent. Honest and heartfelt is enough.
prayer.starter2: "God, if you are real, make yourself real to me."
prayer.starter3: "Jesus, I need you. Help me get through this moment."
prayer.own-words: Or just talk to God in your own words. You do not have to have it figured out.
prayer.hold.label: He meets you exactly where you are.
prayer.affirmation: He meets you exactly where you are.
values.title: Values Alignment Check
values.what-matters.label: What Matters Most
values.what-matters.q: What are the three things in life you care about most?
values.what-matters.hint: Examples: my kids, my faith, my health, being a good person
values.weekly.label: Weekly Alignment
values.weekly.q: Looking at the past week — how aligned were your actions with those three things?
values.off-course.label: What's Off Course
values.off-course.q: Is there one thing you are doing right now that is working against what you care about?
values.small-move.label: One Small Move
values.small-move.q: What is one small thing you could do in the next 24 hours that would move you closer to what you care about?
values.placeholder: Take your time (nothing is saved or transmitted)
values.affirmation: Clarity about what matters is itself a form of calm. You know who you want to be.
sleep.title: Sleep Hygiene Guide
sleep.subtitle: Tap each item to check it off
sleep.tip.1: Set a consistent bedtime and stick to it.
sleep.tip.2: Start dimming lights 1 hour before bed.
sleep.tip.4: Try a calming pre-sleep routine: light reading, gentle stretching, or a warm bath.
sleep.tip.5: 7–9 hours is the research-supported target. If you toss and turn, allow extra time in bed.
sleep.tip.6: If racing thoughts keep you up: try box breathing in bed, or listen to something calm and distracting.
sleep.note: Sleep is the single biggest lever for your ability to handle stress. Prioritize it even when it feels impossible.
movement.title: Movement Prompt
movement.framing: Your body is holding stress. Movement releases it. You do not need a gym.
movement.opt.1: A 10-minute walk outside (even slow, even around the block)
movement.opt.3: Put on a song and move however feels right
movement.opt.4: Do 10 slow squats or 10 wall push-ups — just to move
movement.return.msg: Go do it now. Come back when you are done.
movement.return.sub: This page will be here when you return.
movement.affirmation: Nice work. Your cortisol just dropped a little. That mattered.
journal.title: Journaling
journal.prompt: Write whatever is in your head. Nobody will see this. It does not have to make sense.
journal.secondary.1: What am I most afraid of right now?
journal.secondary.2: What do I wish someone would say to me?
journal.secondary.3: What is one thing I need to let go of today?
journal.timer.label: Timer:
journal.privacy: Your entry is never saved or transmitted — download creates a local file only.
journal.confirm-clear: Clear your journal entry? This cannot be undone.
grounding.title: 5-Senses Grounding
grounding.framing: You are here. Right now. Let's prove that to your nervous system — one sense at a time.
grounding.see.label: 5 — See
grounding.see.prompt: Look around slowly. Name 5 things you can see right now.
grounding.see.placeholder: A lamp, the wall, my hands, a window, a cup...
grounding.touch.label: 4 — Touch
grounding.touch.prompt: Notice 4 things you can physically feel — texture, weight, temperature.
grounding.touch.placeholder: The floor under my feet, the chair beneath me...
grounding.hear.label: 3 — Hear
grounding.hear.prompt: Listen quietly. What are 3 sounds you can hear right now?
grounding.hear.placeholder: Traffic outside, my own breathing, the fan...
grounding.smell.label: 2 — Smell
grounding.smell.prompt: Take a slow breath through your nose. Name 2 things you can smell, even faintly.
grounding.smell.placeholder: Coffee, fresh air, nothing in particular...
grounding.taste.label: 1 — Taste
grounding.taste.prompt: What do you taste right now, even the faintest trace?
grounding.affirmation: You just proved to your brain that you are safe right now — in this moment, in this place.
nutrition.title: Nutrition Guide
nutrition.subtitle: Tap each item to check it off
nutrition.tip.1: Eat something — even small. Your brain needs glucose to think and process emotions.
nutrition.tip.2: Prioritize protein: eggs, chicken, Greek yogurt, legumes. It stabilizes blood sugar and mood.
nutrition.tip.3: Choose whole foods over comfort foods. Processed food spikes then crashes your blood sugar, worsening anxiety.
nutrition.tip.4: Aim for 3 meals today. Skipping meals raises cortisol and makes everything feel harder.
nutrition.tip.5: Limit sugar and refined carbs — they feel comforting in the moment but intensify emotional swings.
nutrition.tip.6: Limit or skip alcohol. It disrupts sleep and keeps cortisol elevated — the opposite of calm.
nutrition.tip.7: Drink water. Dehydration worsens anxiety, brain fog, and emotional dysregulation.
nutrition.note: When your body is undernourished, it is incredibly difficult to think clearly. Feeding yourself is not a luxury right now — it is a calming intervention.
mindfulness.title: Mindfulness Check-In
mindfulness.framing: You don't have to fix what you're feeling. Just notice it. That is the whole practice.
mindfulness.step1.label: Step 1 of 4 — Settle
mindfulness.step1.q: Find a comfortable position. Close your eyes if you'd like.
mindfulness.step1.sub: Take three slow, deep breaths before continuing.
mindfulness.step2.label: Step 2 of 4 — Notice
mindfulness.step2.q: What emotion is present right now?
mindfulness.step2.sub: Don't judge it. Don't fix it. Just name it like you're naming weather outside.
mindfulness.step2.placeholder: e.g. Dread. Sadness. Rage. Numbness. Anxiety. Relief. Nothing.
mindfulness.step3.label: Step 3 of 4 — Get Curious
mindfulness.step3.q: Where do you feel this in your body?
mindfulness.step3.sub: A tight chest? Heavy shoulders? Pit in your stomach? Describe the sensation, not the story.
mindfulness.step3.placeholder: Describe what you physically feel, not what happened or why.
mindfulness.step4.label: Step 4 of 4 — Ride the Wave
mindfulness.step4.q: Just sit with it for 60 seconds. Don't fight it or feed it.
mindfulness.step4.sub: Watch the feeling like a wave. Let it rise, peak, and begin to fall on its own.
mindfulness.hold.label: Just notice. You don't have to do anything.
mindfulness.affirmation: You leaned in instead of running. That takes more courage than most people realize.
